newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London inch up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London inch up in thin trade.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London edged higher in a largely inactive market on Monday with bank stocks recovering some poise after recent weakness, traders said.
In Tokyo the 225-share Nikkei average shed 244.06 points or 1.33 percent to close at 18,085.95.

Sentiment brightened after an auction of land by a former state-owned railway firm fetched more than expected. Traders said bank stocks moved up as the news helped bolster hopes that banks could tackle their bad loans problems.
Sumitomo Bank rose 10 yen from its Tokyo close to 1320 in London by 1445 GMT.
Sanwa Bank was trading at 1,345 yen, up 5 yen from its close in Japan and Asahi Bank 8322T was 3.5 yen higher at 843.5 yen.
But the main focus of attention was on Toyota Motor Corp after a fire at a key parts supplier halted production at all but one of its domestic plants.
Shares in Toyota slipped 15 yen from the Tokyo close to 3,075 by 1438 GMT.
A fire on Saturday at an Aisin Seiki Co Ltd plant halted output of brake parts supplied to Toyota.
